correctness.rationale: If both sides have omissions and one side has at least two, selected witnesses on that side see at least two omissions; any opposite-side neighbor of an omitted vertex on that side also sees an omission in its own clique. Thus only a mixed pair is possible, and an index different from the two omitted indices gives witnesses on both sides when n≥3. With at least two omissions on just one side, in-clique witnesses are impossible and the opposite matching mates are necessary and sufficient. Single omissions and the empty omission always work. The resulting omission generating polynomial is 2(1+w)^t−1+2(n−t)w+n²w²; mapping omitted size k to selected size 2n−k gives the asserted polynomial. Maximal omissions are exactly mixed pairs and, when t≥2, the full matched subset on either side. Smaller unmatched or matched singletons can be extended to mixed pairs; proper matched subsets of size at least two can be extended within their side. This yields the inclusion-minimal polynomial, min/max, and minimum multiplicities, including addition at the coincident exponent when t=2.
residual_risks: General claims rest on the witness argument, not finite replay. No extension to n=2 or to cross edges other than a matching is asserted.

value.rationale: The partial matching interpolates between disconnected cliques and a standard prism. The classification explains the competition between within-clique and cross-clique witnesses, giving a sharp transition at t=3 between equal cardinalities of maximal omissions and an unbounded spread of sizes of inclusion-minimal sets, even on connected prisms. This structural outcome is not captured by the known scalar minimum.
residual_risks: No claim of a new polynomial framework or results outside the stated graph family.
